correctness.rationale: The independent spin flips induce exactly the stated three-state chain. The invariant interval and uniqueness follow from inward drifts, irreducible switching and contraction at least at rate λ under common switching. In stationarity the distributional derivative of each mode flux is a finite measure, so the flux is locally a BV density and the mode measure can only have a singular part at its own isolated drift zero. At that zero no incoming switch can supply an atom, because the other modes' drifts are nonzero there, and the outgoing rate is positive. The total flux is the zero constant by testing across the compact support. Near each endpoint its dominant nonnegative flux q equals the sum of the other two unsigned fluxes. The ratio of either summand to q lies in [0,1]; positive mass from long extremal-mode sojourns and the resulting differential inequalities force q>0 locally. The dominant drift slopes are 2h/a and 2h/b and the outgoing rate is 2γ. Hence in inward distance z the logarithmic derivative is 2γ/(slope·z)+O(1); integration gives a finite positive coefficient with relative O(z) error, and dividing by the drift gives the density exponent. The other modes' densities are smaller by O(z). Both thresholds and stated identities then follow, including the nonzero finite limits at equality. The supplied finite-volume evidence is corroboration, not the continuum proof.
residual_risks: No claim about smoothness across the interior drift zero, vanishing parameter limits or individual-position densities is supported by this endpoint argument.
